source.title: The additive indecomposability of the primes

hypotheses: q is any odd prime; all field and unit norms/expectations use probability measure.
g(0)=0 and E_Fq |g|^2<=1; no pointwise bound.
All multiplicative characters, including principal, are zero at zero.
Literal ordered full binary diagrams, unit data, consistency equations and current-entry propagation of eq:src36.
Zero reconstructed entry kills the whole diagram before division.
Opposite bottom-sibling conjugations; different pairs and diagrams may differ.
For paired comparison l>=2, equal numbers of nonempty paired components, uniform product-equality subgroup law.
The first component-quartet graph has a cycle; b<=3r/4 is a sufficient condition.

claims.proof: report.md section 1; valid subprobability law <=2^(k-1) uniform law
report.md section 2; nonidentity fiber bound plus additive-Fourier Hilbert-Schmidt estimate
report.md section 3; subtract principal contribution before Gauss identity; handle all principal exceptions
report.md section 4; parameter-free nonnegative majorants with both small supremum and bounded total mean
report.md section 5; conditional projection and character relation, including t=1 parallel-edge case
single moment <=3^r; paired bound follows from sections 1-5

strongest_report_claims.claim: For the stated paired diagrams, |E W1 conjugate(W2)|<=16^r(epsilon+q^(-1/4)).
A cycle in the first component-quartet multigraph suffices without the numerical restriction b<=3r/4.
